Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

force verb

make someone do something

also compel, make someone do, be forced to, oblige

classical

Ter. And. 780–781: coāctus lēgibus eam uxōrem dūcet
Verg. Ecl. 2.7: morī mē dēnique cōgēs?

cōgō, cōgere, coēgī, coāctum

verb, third conjugation, with the accusative and an infinitive or ut

force, compel

coāctus, against one’s will; “I was forced to” is coāctus sum with an infinitive.

Examples

  • nīl nostrī miserēre? morī mē dēnique cōgēs?

    have you no pity for me? will you drive me to my death in the end?Verg. Ecl. 2.7

  • hujus igitur bellī ego particeps et socius et adjūtor esse cōgor …?

    am I, then, to be forced to be a partner, an ally and a helper in this war …?Cic. Att. 9.10.5

  • Coāctus lēgibus eam uxōrem dūcet.

    The law will force him to marry her.Ter. And. 780–781

Other words

  • compellō, compellere, compulī, compulsum — drive (someone) to, force

    verb, third conjugation, with ad or in · also used · classical · Cic. Marc. 13: ad arma (Lewis & Short)

    Of driving someone into doing something: aliquem ad aliquid compellere.

See also force, make.

SourcesLewis & Short: cogo · Lewis & Short: compello
